title: cmate-orchestrate dispatch report v1
description: Report printed to stdout and written to dispatch-report.json by the cmate-orchestrate dispatch runner. Closed schema: an unknown field is a contract violation, not something a reader may ignore. It records the supervised execution of an already-approved plan: per-wave dispatch, worker supervision, the wave barrier, and the verification gate. Worker completion and verification success are reported as separate facts and are never conflated. Since Skill 0.9.0 the verification verdict may come either from CommandMate's execution contract (`commandmate wait --verify`'s exit code) or from the profile-baseline fallback; the field set and the meaning of every enum value are identical in both modes, so a reader (the merge and UAT runners) needs no change. Which mode ran is stated in limitations/blocking_reasons and in summary_markdown.

status.description: success: every wave dispatched, every worker completed, every verification passed. partial: some progress but the loop stopped early (worker failure, timeout, verification failure, a prompt awaiting a human, or drift). failure: nothing was dispatched.

stop_reason.description: Why the loop stopped. completed: all waves finished and passed. human_required: a worker raised a prompt and the loop halted without auto-responding. dispatch_error also covers the pre-dispatch and version-gate/verdict stops: open_questions (an issue in the plan still carries an unanswered planner question and --allow-questions was not set, so nothing was dispatched), contract_unsupported (the CLI has no execution contract and --contract-mode require refused to fall back) and verification_not_judged (verification exited 99, meaning the run ended error/cancelled and no gate judged the work). The rest name the first blocking condition.

human_required.description: True when the loop halted for a human: a worker raised a prompt, verification returned no verdict at all (exit 99), or the plan carried an unanswered planner question that only an edit to the issue body can resolve. None of the three is resolvable by re-dispatching. When true, no prompt was auto-answered unless auto_yes was set.

out_dir.description: Directory the dispatch artifacts were written to. Null when nothing was written.

auto_yes.description: Whether Auto Yes was enabled. Default off: a detected prompt halts for a human rather than being answered.

drift_checks.description: Pre-mutation drift re-checks (branch/HEAD/worktree/permission), one entry per probe, tagged with the wave they guarded.

blocking.description: Whether a failure of this check blocks dispatch. A non-blocking failure becomes a limitation, not a halt.

waves.description: Ordered waves, in plan order. A wave is only present if the loop reached it; a wave present with an empty dispatched list means drift halted it before any send.

checks.description: Six checks since Skill 0.16.0; 0.15.x and earlier wrote five (everything but `verification_recorded`). The range is 5..6 so both keep validating — an additive widening, which is why dispatch_schema_version stays 1.

dispatched.description: Issues actually sent in this wave. Never longer than max_parallel.

all_workers_completed.description: Every dispatched worker reached the completed state. This alone never advances the wave.

all_verifications_passed.description: Every worker of this wave reached a passing verification verdict — the exit code of commandmate wait --verify under a contract, or a clean profile-baseline re-run without one.

advanced.description: The next wave was allowed to dispatch. True only when workers completed AND verifications passed.

task_id.description: Under an execution contract this is the task id `commandmate send --contract` returned, so the run can be traced back to the recorded task. Without one the public CLI has no task id and the field carries the CommandMate worktree id instead. Null when the worker was never dispatched.

worker_state.description: completed is worker completion only; it is not verification success. Those are gated separately. `timeout` means THIS RUNNER stopped waiting (`commandmate wait` returned exit 124); it does not mean the worker died — see worker_liveness for which of the two a given timeout was.

worker_liveness.description: OPTIONAL. What `commandmate capture --json` said about this worker AT THE MOMENT its `commandmate wait` timed out (Issue #179). `--wait-timeout` bounds one wait, not the worker, so a timeout is either 'the runner stopped watching' (the worker is still going and may still commit) or 'the worker stopped' — and re-dispatching on the first reading puts a second worker on top of work the first is finishing. The probe is made ONCE per timeout, never polled. ABSENT means no probe was made — the worker did not time out, or the record was transcribed from a prior attempt — and must NOT be read as 'the worker was not alive', for the same reason an absent gate `origin` is not `repo`. Added optionally, so reports written before this field keep validating and dispatch_schema_version stays 1.

code.description: wait_window_exhausted: the capture showed a live worker, so the WAIT WINDOW ran out and the recovery is to wait and re-judge in place (--reverify), never to re-dispatch. worker_stalled: the capture answered and showed no evidence of a running worker. worker_liveness_unreadable: the capture failed or its output could not be read, so NEITHER state was measured — it is never rounded to one of the other two. The same code is recorded as a blocking reason.

session_status.description: The capture's own `sessionStatus`, transcribed. Null when it was absent or unreadable.

elapsed_seconds.description: Wall-clock seconds between the send that opened this worker's supervision and the liveness probe. Against `--wait-timeout` it is what shows whether one turn simply outgrew the window.

verification.description: The verdict that judged this worker. Recorded for EVERY worker that reached one, independently of whether the rest of the wave completed (Issue #83): the wave barrier decides whether the next wave dispatches, never whether this fact is written down. `note` never states a verification result this object does not — the sentence a human reads is rendered from these fields.

report_schema_version.description: Version of the verification report the worker produced. Always null in practice: the profile baseline produces no versioned document, and CommandMate's verification run document carries no schema version either. Kept so a future versioned report can be recorded without a schema change.

outcome.description: pass and fail are verdicts. not_run means NOTHING JUDGED THIS: no verification ran for this worker at all (it raised a prompt, was never dispatched, or its wait failed for infrastructure reasons), or the verification run itself ended error/cancelled (exit 99) so no gate reached a verdict. not_run is never a pass, and it is deliberately not a fail either — 'we could not judge' must not be re-instructed as 'we judged it and it failed'. Conversely, a verdict that WAS reached is recorded even when the worker did not complete (Issue #83): exit 21 is the work-evidence gate judging and failing, so it is `fail`, not 'nothing judged it'. Worker completion is reported separately in worker_state and the two are never conflated.

origin.description: OPTIONAL. Where this gate came from: `issue` when the issue's own ```acceptance-gates block named the id under `require:`, `repo` when the gate is part of the repository's common set and the issue said nothing about it. Added for #97's PR evidence, which must be able to say how many of the green gates ran FOR THIS ISSUE rather than only that ten gates were green. Measured: `commandmate wait --verify`'s `GATE <id> PASS|FAIL` line carries no provenance, so the value is DECIDED by the dispatch runner from the ids it resolved out of the plan and wrote into the contract — deterministic, and it fixes the reading that a declared-but-not-required gate is `repo`. ABSENT means the origin was not recorded (a runner older than this field, or the fallback baseline path) and must NOT be read as `repo`, for the same reason `not_run` is rounded to neither pass nor fail.

gates.description: The gates that judged this work, transcribed from `commandmate wait --verify`'s `GATE <id> PASS|FAIL` stdout lines (falling back to the confirming `verify --json` run's failing gates on exit 20). Empty when nothing was judged (not_run), when the CLI printed no GATE lines, or on the fallback baseline path (whose commands are already named in checks). This is what lets the report alone answer WHAT a pass was based on (#1678 B-5). Since 0.16.0 an empty list on a contract PASS is itself reported — a `verification_gates_unrecorded` limitation plus a line in `checks` — so an unattributed pass is visible instead of reading as a pass with nothing to show (Issue #83).

excerpt.description: Redacted excerpt of the prompt for a human. Never the raw terminal, never a secret.
